title: Six quarters of sequential growth
body:
## The IPO Baseline

When Astera Labs opened on the NASDAQ at $52.56 on March 20, 2024 — 46 percent above the $36 IPO price — it was carrying an implicit obligation: prove that connectivity silicon, not just accelerator GPUs, would define the margin profile of the AI infrastructure cycle. The first-day pop, which valued the company at roughly $9.5 billion at the offering and north of $13 billion at the close, was less a celebration of a finished story than a wager on a pipeline. Six consecutive quarters of sequential revenue growth, extending from late 2024 through to the Q1 2026 guidance issued in February 2026, would discharge that obligation in numbers.

## Q4 FY2024: The First Benchmark

The quarter that established the sequential-growth baseline — Q4 FY2024, reported [February 10, 2025](https://www.asteralabs.com/news/) — came in at $141.1 million, up 25 percent from the prior quarter and 179 percent year-over-year. Full-year FY2024 revenue landed at $396.3 million, a 242 percent increase over FY2023's $115.8 million. Aries PCIe retimers had driven the majority of that gain, but the Q4 print carried a signal that would prove important: Taurus Smart Cable Modules for Ethernet arrived "strongly in Q4," as Jitendra Mohan put it in the earnings release.

The CEO framed what was coming with unusual specificity:

> "We expect 2025 to be a breakout year as we enter a new phase of growth driven by revenue from all four of our product families to support a diverse set of customers and platforms. This includes our flagship Scorpio Fabric products for head-node PCIe connectivity and backend AI accelerator scale-up clustering." — Jitendra Mohan, Q4 FY2024 earnings, [February 10, 2025](https://www.asteralabs.com/news/)

GAAP gross margin in Q4 FY2024 was 74.0 percent — already a level associated with software-style economics in silicon — with GAAP diluted EPS of $0.14.

## Q1 FY2025: Off-Consensus Entry

The first quarter of FY2025, reported [May 6, 2025](https://www.asteralabs.com/news/), printed $159.4 million — a 13 percent sequential increase and 144 percent year-over-year. More significant than the revenue figure was that the result exceeded guidance on gross margin and earnings per share. Mohan characterised the strategic position in terms that would become the company's standing refrain:

> "Our design wins across AI platforms, expanding portfolio with increasing value for customers, and significant traction with Scorpio fabric solutions strategically position us as a critical connectivity supplier for the entire AI rack." — Jitendra Mohan, Q1 FY2025, [May 6, 2025](https://www.asteralabs.com/news/)

GAAP gross margin expanded to 74.9 percent. GAAP diluted EPS moved to $0.18. The sequential growth rate was the lowest of the next five quarters, but the important structural fact was that Q1 maintained the upward trajectory into what is typically the seasonally softer period of the enterprise infrastructure calendar.

## Q2 FY2025: Volume Production Milestone

Q2 FY2025, reported [August 5, 2025](https://www.asteralabs.com/news/), delivered $191.9 million — a 20 percent sequential increase and 150 percent year-over-year. The quarter crossed a threshold: PCIe 6 product portfolio entered volume production for customized rack-scale AI systems, and Scorpio Fabric Switches added multiple new design wins.

> "Astera Labs delivered strong financial results in Q2 with sequential revenue growth of 20 percent, driving meaningful upside to earnings and cash flow from operations." — Jitendra Mohan, Q2 FY2025, [August 5, 2025](https://www.asteralabs.com/news/)

The gross margin inflected materially: GAAP gross margin reached 75.8 percent, the first quarter at a level that would characterise the full-year FY2025 average. Operating cash flow for Q2 alone reached $135.4 million — a record at the time and a figure that alone exceeded the company's quarterly R&D spending, signalling that the operating-leverage model was functioning as designed. GAAP diluted EPS doubled quarter-over-quarter to $0.29.

## Q3 FY2025: The $200 Million Threshold

The third quarter of FY2025, reported [November 4, 2025](https://www.asteralabs.com/news/astera-labs-announces-financial-results-for-the-third-quarter-of-fiscal-year-2025/), was the first in Astera's public history to exceed $200 million: revenue came in at $230.6 million, up 20 percent sequentially and 104 percent year-over-year. GAAP gross margin reached 76.2 percent, the peak of the sequential run.

Mohan attributed the upside to convergent demand across the portfolio — signal conditioning, Smart Cable Modules, and switch fabric — and used the Q3 print to introduce the next strategic move:

> "Looking into Q4, we anticipate continued PCIe 6 momentum alongside robust growth from our Taurus Ethernet SCMs. We remain focused on our rack-scale vision, which is further strengthened by the proposed acquisition of aiXscale Photonics, which we believe will support our customers' technology roadmaps and increase our market reach beyond copper interconnects." — Jitendra Mohan, Q3 FY2025, [November 4, 2025](https://www.asteralabs.com/news/)

The photonics acquisition signal was new. Embedded in the Q3 commentary, it foreshadowed that Astera was already looking beyond the copper-interconnect footprint that had delivered the margin expansion.

## Q4 FY2025: Structural-Margin Demonstration

The Q4 FY2025 print, released [February 10, 2026](https://www.asteralabs.com/news/), was the one that resolved the investor thesis in a single line: $270.6 million of revenue, 75.6 percent GAAP gross margin, $0.25 GAAP diluted EPS, $0.58 non-GAAP diluted EPS. Sequential growth of 17 percent. Year-over-year growth of 92 percent.

| Quarter | Revenue ($M) | Sequential Growth | GAAP GM | GAAP Dil. EPS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q4 FY2024 | 141.1 | +25% | 74.0% | $0.14 |
| Q1 FY2025 | 159.4 | +13% | 74.9% | $0.18 |
| Q2 FY2025 | 191.9 | +20% | 75.8% | $0.29 |
| Q3 FY2025 | 230.6 | +20% | 76.2% | $0.50 |
| Q4 FY2025 | 270.6 | +17% | 75.6% | $0.25 |

*Sources: Astera Labs quarterly earnings press releases, February 2025 – February 2026*

For the full year, FY2025 revenue reached $852.5 million, 115 percent ahead of FY2024's $396.3 million. GAAP gross margin for the year was 75.7 percent. The full-year characterisation from Mohan was unambiguous:

> "Astera Labs delivered strong financial results in Q4 with revenue growing by 17% sequentially to a new record level of $270.6 million, highlighting a stellar 2025 with full-year revenue growth of 115% year-over-year. The market opportunity for our Intelligent Connectivity Platform continues to grow rapidly, encompassing multiple product lines, physical media, form factors, and protocols for standard and custom applications." — Jitendra Mohan, Q4 FY2025, [February 10, 2026](https://www.asteralabs.com/news/)

The stock price, which opened its public life at $52.56 on the first trading day in March 2024, traded through a wide range across the subsequent seven quarters as AI-server cycle expectations oscillated. Near the snapshot date of May 23, 2026, ALAB remained a high-multiple connectivity-silicon name, with the debate centred on whether FY2026 sustains the architecture-transition demand.

## The Operating-Leverage Signature

The number that may matter most to a long-cycle investor is not the revenue figure or even the gross margin, but the relationship between operating cash flow and R&D spending. FY2025 operating cash flow was $319.3 million. Total FY2025 operating expenses — including R&D, sales and marketing, and general and administrative — were $471.8 million. Even if one attributes roughly half of that to engineering and product development, the operating cash flow line materially exceeds the R&D investment required to produce the next generation of design-ins. That is the operating-leverage signature of a connectivity-silicon company that has moved from design-in execution to volume realisation.

The balance sheet reinforces that structural health: $167.6 million of cash and equivalents plus $1.02 billion of marketable securities totalled $1.187 billion of liquid at December 31, 2025, against essentially no debt. The capital structure imposes no near-term financing pressure regardless of AI-capex cycle timing.

## What Q1 2026 Implies

The Q1 FY2026 guidance issued with the Q4 print — $286 to $297 million of revenue, $0.36 to $0.38 GAAP diluted EPS — implied a 7.7 percent sequential increase at the midpoint of $291.5 million. That guidance range, if met, would extend the sequential-growth streak to seven straight quarters and lift the annualised run-rate above $1.1 billion. It would also arrive in the quarter when CFO succession was completing, with Desmond Lynch, formerly SVP Finance and CFO at Rambus, taking over from Mike Tate effective March 2026.

The cumulative observation is this: across seven public quarters Astera has demonstrated uninterrupted sequential revenue growth, gross margins that stabilised above 75 percent GAAP on a structural rather than incidental basis, GAAP profitability in all but the first partial-year period, and operating cash flow that comfortably exceeds R&D spend. The compound sequential growth rates — 25, 13, 20, 20, 17 percent — are not uniform, but they are unbroken. For a connectivity-silicon company building through one of the fastest AI infrastructure cycles in history, the absence of a single down quarter through changing platform generations is itself the data.
